newsitem.title: USA: Study cites economic gains from U.S.-UK air pact.
newsitem.headline: Study cites economic gains from U.S.-UK air pact.

text.p: An "open skies" aviation agreement between the United States and Britain would bring substantial gains for the U.S. economy, according to a study conducted for American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp.

American has been a leading supporter of a free market accord, which the U.S. Transportation Department says is a prerequisite for approval of American's proposed transatlantic marketing alliance with British Airways Plc.

The study by consulting firm Roberts Roach & Associates said an "open skies" pact and the alliance that would follow would boost the U.S. economy by $108 billion over five years, create 152,000 new jobs and increase U.S.-British air service by 86 percent.

It said that by replacing the current restrictive accord, more U.S. airlines would enter the London market and the market share American and BA now hold would be reduced, not increased to monopoly size as some critics contend.
The study also said there were adequate landing slots at London's Heathrow airport to handle additional U.S. flights.
U.S. officials on November 7 proposed to start new "open skies" negotiations with Britain the first week in December.
Talks over the past two years have all ended in failure.
